name: Group Theory

papers.title: Non-Amenability of Small Overlap Semigroups
papers.abstract: We prove that every semigroup admitting a presentation satisfying the small overlap condition $C(3)$ is neither left nor right reversible, unless it is the free semigroup on one generator. Consequently, all such semigroups outside this exception are both left and right non-amenable. We also show the optimality of this result, giving examples of $C(2)$ semigroups that are left and right amenable. Our proof makes use of semigroup diagrams, extending the results of Remmers who first introduced the methods as a means of studying small overlap semigroups. We also compare this to the known result that the $C(7)$ condition in groups implies hyperbolicity which then implies non-amenability (excluding the elementary cases). We establish that, for $m\geq 4$, a strongly $C(m)$ semigroup presentation induces an enveloping group presentation satisfying the small cancellation condition $C(2m-6)$, and show that this bound is sharp.

papers.title: Fixed points for actions of automorphism groups of free products on ${\rm CAT(0)}$ spaces
papers.abstract: We study fixed-point properties of automorphism groups of free products acting on complete ${\rm CAT(0)}$ spaces. Under the assumption of certain fixed-point properties of the free factors, we obtain lower bounds on the smallest dimension in which automorphism groups can act on a complete ${\rm CAT(0)}$ space without a global fixed point.

papers.title: A note on characterization of S4 x C2^n
papers.abstract: For every non-negative integer n, we characterize S4 x C2^n by its poset of isomorphic classes of subgroups. This provides an infinite family of counterexamples to the conjectures posed by Tarnauceanu in [8] and [9].

papers.title: Normal abelian subgroups of order 5^6 in finite 5-groups
papers.abstract: A finite 5-group containing an abelian subgroup of order 5^6 has a normal abelian subgroup of that order. If the given subgroup is elementary abelian, the normal subgroup can be chosen elementary abelian. This resolves n=6, the last open case of both parts of Problem~21.51 of the Kourovka Notebook for p=5. Together with earlier results, it follows that 1\le n\le 6 is the exact range in which each assertion holds for every finite 5-group at subgroup order 5^n. In a minimal counterexample, five conjugate abelian subgroups generate a group of class at most three. In class two we construct invariant isotropic subgroups for the commutator pairing. In class three the Jacobi identity produces a nonzero plane cubic over the field of five elements. The five conjugate subgroups give five distinct singular points spanning the plane, which forces the cubic to vanish.

papers.title: On some problems regarding a group-theoretical generalization of the Gauss formula
papers.abstract: In \cite{FT23}, we introduced the group-theoretical function $f(G) = \frac{1}{|G|}\sum_{H \le G} |\Aut(H)|$ for a finite group $G$ and posed three open problems concerning its values on noncyclic groups. In this note, we provide complete solutions to all three problems.

papers.title: Stable finiteness and combination theorems for Hughes-free embeddings
papers.abstract: We show that all group algebras of Higman's group and Deligne's group are stably finite. We also study when the Hughes-free embeddability property is closed under taking graphs of groups, and give a positive answer when the edge maps are retractions or injective on Abelianisations. As a consequence we obtain that fundamental groups of graphs of torsion-free Abelian groups, graph products of locally indicable Hughes-free embeddable groups, and fundamental groups of graphs of free groups with cyclic edge groups are Hughes-free embeddable.

papers.title: A formula to construct all elements of finite order in Riordan matrix groups
papers.abstract: We characterize the elements of finite order in the Riordan group over the complex field by providing explicit conditions on their entries. Our main result generalizes a previous characterization of involutions to arbitrary finite orders and gives a constructive procedure to determine all Riordan matrices of a prescribed finite order from a suitable choice of parameters. The proof relies on an inductive analysis of the principal submatrices. We further derive consequences for the Lagrange subgroup and the group of formal power series under composition, obtaining a characterization of finite-order series and a constructive description of the solutions to associated functional equations.

papers.title: Tensor products of finite groups without compatibility conditions are finite
papers.abstract: It has been an open question whether Inassaridze's tensor product $G\otimes H$ is finite whenever $G$ and $H$ are finite. In this paper, we answer this question in the affirmative, and, as a consequence, we prove that the low dimensional nonabelian homology groups $H_i(G,A)$, $i=0,1$, are finite whenever $G$ and $A$ are finite. We achieve this by introducing a much more general tensor product $G\bt H$, defined for groups acting on themselves and on each other by arbitrary automorphisms, with no compatibility conditions, and subject only to the two defining relations of the nonabelian tensor product. We prove that $G\bt H$ is finite whenever $G$ and $H$ are finite. Since the nonabelian tensor product of Brown and Loday, Inassaridze's tensor product and the box-tensor product are all quotients or special cases of $G\bt H$, this brings the finiteness results for all these tensor products under one umbrella.

papers.title: On the theorem of Bryce and Cossey about hereditary Fitting formations of finite soluble groups
papers.abstract: Recall that a class of groups $\mathfrak{F}$ is called $D_\mathfrak{X}$-closed if it contains every group $G = MN$ where $M$ and $N$ are normal $\mathfrak{F}$-subgroups of $G$ and $M\cap N\in \mathfrak{X}$. We prove that a hereditary formation of $\omega$-soluble groups is an $n$-multiply $\omega$-local formation if and only if it is a $D_{\mathfrak{N}^n_\omega}$-closed formation. As corollaries we obtain the theorem of Bryce and Cossey about saturation of hereditary Fitting formations of finite soluble groups and its extension to the class of all $\pi$-soluble groups, as well as the criterion for a formation of soluble groups to be $n$-multiply local.

papers.title: The type I conjecture for locally compact groups acting on trees
papers.abstract: We prove that a closed group of automorphisms acting minimally on a locally finite tree and two-transitively on its boundary is uniformly admissible, hence of type I. This solves Nebbia's conjecture in a strong form. Together with the work of Caprace, Kalantar and Monod, this shows that for every closed nonamenable subgroup $G$ of $\mathrm{Aut}(T)$ acting minimally on a locally finite tree $T$, $G$ is of type I if and only if the action on $\partial T$ is two-transitive. The key ingredient is the following operator algebraic result: if the projections of two atomic von Neumann algebras $A_1, A_2$ have integer traces, then every amenable amalgamated free product $A_1 \ast_B A_2$ with $B$ atomic is of type I.

papers.title: A non-Morse relatively Anosov group
papers.abstract: We construct a relatively Anosov group that is not relatively Morse.

papers.title: On Zappa--Szép products of multiplicative racks
papers.abstract: We study Zappa--Sz\'ep products of multiplicative racks, namely monoids equipped with compatible rack operations. We characterize multiplicative rack structures on Zappa--Sz\'ep products of monoids and prove that every exact factorization of multiplicative racks induces a canonical exact factorization of their universal groups. We also establish exact factorizations of groups of units and cancellative quotients, show that reduction modulo units yields a direct product, and obtain consequences for Ore localization. We then generalize Bianchi's construction using augmentations from partially multiplicative racks into arbitrary multiplicative racks and establish a reconstruction theorem for multiplicative racks with suitable unital ideals. We investigate the interaction between unital ideals and exact factorizations, and characterize Zappa--Sz\'ep factorizations of generalized Bianchi-type multiplicative racks. Finally, we use a layered central-quotient construction to obtain finite and infinite non-cancellative multiplicative quandles with non-group factors and nontrivial Zappa--Sz\'ep actions, all directly indecomposable as monoids.

papers.title: Extensions of congruent monotileable (and amenable) groups
papers.abstract: A monotile of a countable group $G$ is a finite subset $F \subseteq G$ that tiles $G$, namely $G=\bigsqcup_{c\in C} c F$, for some set of centers $C\subseteq G$. The group $G$ is called congruent monotileable (CM) if it admits an exhaustive sequence of monotiles $(F_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ such that each $F_{n+1}$ is teselated by $F_n$. If moreover $G$ is amenable and the sequence $(F_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ is Folner, we say $G$ is congruent monotileable amenable (CMA). In this work we observe that the classes of CM and CMA groups are stable under group extensions satisfying a certain technical condition, which we call $stepwise$ $monotileability$, and which is a weaker version of the notion of $X$-$monotileability$ introduced by Dikranjan $et al$. Our condition also includes central extensions previously considered by Gao, Jackson, Seward for CM groups, and by Cecchi Bernales, Cortez for CMA groups. We show that this condition is satisfied by semidirect products of the form $G\wr H$, provided $G$ and $H$ are CM/CMA groups, and also by extensions of locally finite groups by CM/CMA groups. This furnishes new examples of CM and CMA groups. In particular, we provide the first examples of finitely generated CMA groups which are neither solvable nor residually finite.

papers.title: Enhanced Helgason-Johnson bounds for classical groups of type $B$
papers.abstract: This paper improves the Helgason-Johnson bound in 1969 for non-Hermitian real classical groups of type $B$.

papers.title: Measurable equidecomposability and the Banach--Ruziewicz problem over locally compact non-Archimedean valued fields
papers.abstract: We prove a measurable analogue of the Banach--Tarski paradox over locally compact non-Archimedean valued fields. Let $\mathbb K$ be the completion of a number field at a non-Archimedean place (e.g., $\mathbb K=\mathbb Q_p$) and $n\ge 2$. Then any two bounded Haar measurable subsets of $\mathbb K^n$ with nonempty interior and equal Haar measure can be cut into finitely many Haar measurable pieces and rearranged into each other by elements of a certain countable group $\Gamma$ of affine isometries. We also show that the Haar measure is, up to a constant factor, the unique nonzero finitely additive $\Gamma$-invariant measure on the bounded Haar measurable subsets of $\mathbb K^n$, which solves a $p$-adic version of the Banach--Ruziewicz problem. Both results follow from the fact that the action of $\Gamma$ on $\mathbb K^n$ is expanding, a property closely related to the spectral gap. For $n=1$ and arbitrary characteristic, we obtain analogous results when the residue field is not prime, using a countable group of isometries that are not necessarily affine.

papers.title: The inductive Galois-McKay conjecture for groups of Lie type C
papers.abstract: We prove the inductive Galois-McKay conjecture for the symplectic groups. A key result is the determination of the character fields of the irreducible characters of the extensions of the symplectic group by field automorphisms. Two main ingredients for this are the theory of Brauer trees and the generalized Gelfand-Graev characters.

papers.title: On infinite torsion of abelian varieties over large algebraic fields of positive characteristic
papers.abstract: Let $A$ be a non-zero abelian variety defined over a finitely generated field $F$. A conjecture of Geyer and Jarden [GJ78] asserts that for every $\sigma\in \mathrm{Gal}(F^{sep}/F)$ outside a set of Haar measure zero, there exist infinitely many primes $\ell$ such that the $\ell$-torsion subgroup of $A(F^{sep}(\sigma))$ is non-zero (or equivalently, the torsion subgroup of $A(F^{sep}(\sigma))$ is infinite), where $F^{sep}(\sigma)$ denotes the subfield of $F^{sep}$ fixed by $\sigma$. While this conjecture remains open when $\mathrm{Char}(F)>0$, we establish a new case under the assumptions of $\mathrm{End}(A)=\mathbb{Z}$ and the connectedness of the algebraic monodromy groups attached to $A/F$.

papers.title: Spectral reciprocity for reductive groups
papers.abstract: For every finite subgroup $\Gamma\subset\operatorname{SU}(2)$, every connected compact or connected complex reductive group $G$, and every finite central subgroup $B\subset Z(G)$, we construct a degree-preserving linear Fourier isomorphism between the polynomial class modules of $(G,B)$ and $((G/B)^\vee,\widehat B)$. The transform exchanges central twists with characters of the actual grades and preserves the invariant polynomial contributions of the full centralizers. In degree zero it yields central-coefficient reciprocity under the Poincar\'e pairing on $S^3/\Gamma$. In particular, $\Gamma$ admits equally many conjugacy classes of homomorphisms into $G$ and its Langlands dual, which verifies a conjecture of Kojima and Tachikawa.

papers.title: On the Orthogonal Group of Quadratic Modules
papers.abstract: We classify the conjugacy classes of isometries in the orthogonal group of regular quadratic modules over Artinian local rings with finite residue fields, provided that the characteristic is odd and coprime to the order of the isometry. (More generally, the same classification holds over Henselian local rings with finite residue fields, such as the ring of $p$-adic integers.) The main idea is to lift results over finite fields to local rings by using the Henselian property. By applying these results to the residue class rings $\mathbb{Z}/(p^l)$, we also obtain a classification of the conjugacy classes of isometries of discriminant forms, under the condition that the order of the discriminant form is odd and coprime to the order of the isometry.
